title: Steinitz against von Bardeleben, Hastings 1895
outcomes: Predicts the key moves of a real game (the pawn break, the knight entry, the quiet queen move, the discovered check, the rook offer) before seeing them
Names the core skill that decides each of the five moments
Says where the engine at depth 16 shows the game turning, and that it came before the sacrifices

steps.text: **Steinitz (White) against von Bardeleben (Black), Hastings, 17 August 1895.** An Italian Game in which most minor pieces are traded early. Black never castles, and his king is still in the centre when the attack starts. You will predict five White moves before you see them. Each answer is checked against the engine at depth 16, which is evidence, not proof. Watch what each move prepares for the next.

steps.text: **Skills at work.** *Attacking a king in the centre*: White opened lines and brought every piece. *Pawn breaks and levers*: 17.d5, a pawn offered to open two files. *The quiet move in a combination*: 20.Qg4. *Discovered attacks and checks*: 21.Ng5+. *Deflection*: 22.Rxe7+. By the engine's depth-16 numbers the game turned earlier, at 16...c6. Revisit any skill that felt unfamiliar.
